paragraph: Edgewater's single-family market is thin, with 6 sales over six months and a median a hair under $1.1 million on mostly three-bedroom colonials and contemporaries. Median days on market ran 68.5 and the sale-to-list ratio came in at 0.979, so sellers here are okay with waiting for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast. Condos and townhouses are the real market, 75 sales at a median of $625,000, typically two bedrooms and two baths, with about a third of those closings being townhouses rather than stacked units. Sales ran from $236,000 to $2,137,500 because this tier covers both Hudson River waterfront buildings with views and older inland complexes off River Road, so the median is the number to anchor on. At 36 days and a 0.988 ratio, well-priced units are moving, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Monthly medians bounce with the mix rather than trending, and July closings held at 13 with a median of $649,000, which is resilience where a summer plateau would be normal. Deciding between tiers comes down to whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance waterfront living of a condo or townhouse.
